title: SLO-aware shard gating and cost cap for audit ingest pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Add an SLO-aware admission/gating layer to the audit ingestion pipeline that enforces per-tenant shard caps, preserves high-priority admin/SSO/SAML events, and automatically routes excess volume to a cost-optimized cold path. Motivation stems from repeated spikes in audit volume during multi-tenant batch operations and SSO sync windows that inflated storage and indexing costs without preserving SLA for security-sensitive events.

Scope: implement runtime shard-gating controller that: (1) consumes real-time ingestion telemetry (ingest QPS, per-shard queue depth, indexing lag, hot-shard CPU), (2) applies rules for event prioritization (admin/SAML/priv-change are highest), (3) enforces soft/hard caps per tenant with configurable policies (throttle, drop/index-minimal, cold-path), and (4) emits compensating backpressure signals upstream (producer throttles / retry guidance). Policy config should be available via Console (per-tenant quotas + priority mapping) and surfaced in RBAC v2 so admins can opt into different retention tiers.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Prefers correctness of high-value security events over strict FIFO ingestion ordering; some lower-priority audit events may be redirected to coldstore with longer indexing windows.
- Tight coupling with RBAC v2 required to reliably tag privileged events; we will rely on RBAC metadata added at ingress (authz context header).
- Need to avoid creating a single-point-of-failure in the admission controller; it will be implemented as a distributed controller with local fast-path decisions and periodic central policy sync.

Success metrics: reduce unexpected storage growth during spikes by 45% while keeping 99.9% of privileged events indexed within SLO (indexing_latency_p50 < 3s, p99 < 30s).
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller deployed to staging and can enforce per-tenant soft/hard caps
Privileged admin/SSO/SAML events preserved and indexed within defined SLOs in 99.9% of cases
Cold-path routing verified: lower-priority events appear in coldstore and are queryable within defined retention SLA
Console exposes per-tenant cap and priority mapping, tied to RBAC v2 roles
End-to-end tests and chaos tests (ingest spike) validate controller does not cause data loss for privileged events
Playbook documenting operator runbook for thresholds, emergency lift, and rollback is published (Confluence link included)
